 ‘War’ Season 1 Episode 7 Recap: Rumble Boy 
 The first season of War on HBO ends with the bitter Morgan Henderson ( Dominic West )/Carla Duval ( Sienna Miller ) divorce case wrapping up in an unpredictable manner — and with a resilient Johnny Warren ( Archie Renaux ) making one last case for himself at Taylor & Byrne…
 **Spoilers for War Season 1 Episode 8 “Partners,” now streaming on HBO Max** 
 In the War Season 1 finale, Johnny finally convinces Flora Monroe (Rose Williams) to testify in the divorce proceedings by showing her the torn up letter that Morgan wanted to give Carla earlier in the season. However, instead of confirming that she was a paid honey trap, she flips the whole case on its head by revealing the truth. Yes, she seduced Morgan as a favor to Carla, but she also slept with him because she wanted to sleep with him. The money that Johnny gave her went to her mother’s conservatory, yes, but wasn’t hush money in her mind. Finally, she reveals that Johnny was working for Cathcarts and not Taylor & Byrne when he made this underhanded play. Most importantly, though, she reveals that Morgan wanted to settle with Carla earlier in the proceedings. She reads the letter St. John Smallwood (Pip Torrens) tore up.
 As the judge deliberates, Morgan and Carla meet on their own. They go behind their lawyers’ backs and decide to a 50/50 settlement of the funds and shared custody of Gabe (Aran Murphy). However, that’s not the end of the tale…
 In the final scenes, we not only see where Morgan and Carla end up, but we learn that Johnny is hatching one last plan to get back into the fold at Taylor & Byrne. Will Johnny rejoin married partners Nicholas Taylor (James McArdle) and Serena Byrne (Phoebe Fox)? Does Serena ever have her baby? What’s next for the world of HBO’s War ?
 Photo: HBO 
 War Season 1 Ending Explained: Is Johnny back at Taylor & Byrne? Does Serena have her baby?
 In the final scenes of War Season 1, Johnny Warren returns to the sleek offices of Taylor & Byrne to apologize for being the mole and to beg for his job back. However, before we learn if Nicholas and Serena will take him back, she goes into labor. 
 “We don’t see Serena give birth, by the way,” War star Phoebe Fox told DECIDER. “But a lot of the time when you do see women give birth it’s made out to be this like, ah, it’s an emergency! Which it’s just not like that.”
 “I filmed up until four weeks before the [real life] baby came, so I was a bit fed up by the end, honestly,” she added.
 “Timed out so perfectly though, didn’t it?” Archie Renaux said. 
 “No, we had to finish on time. So the producers can thank me for that,” Fox teased.
 That said, given that War Season 2 is in production, can we expect Johnny will return to help out/cause chaos in the next season?
 “The thing we’ve been saying is that no one’s ever out of play because in a world where you can spy for one firm and work for another and get fired or get a bad reference or screw up in New York,” War creator George Kay told DECIDER. “Johnny Warren’s like a cat with nine lives.” 
 “And he was never guilty of ineptitude,” War director Ben Taylor said. “He’s talented and he’s skillful and he can be useful. So I think at that level there’s always going to be a future role.” 
 Archie Renaux stayed mum on his character’s future on the show. “I can’t comment on that, obviously,” he said, but he did explain why Johnny would ultimately prefer working at Taylor & Byrne over Cathcarts. 
 “There are more people like him there than at somewhere like Cathcarts, the youngsters. He builds a good relationship with Molly, played by Emma Laird… Shaheen’s character Saeed,” Renaux said. “He sees a lot more of himself in these characters. “
 “It’s cooler. It’s sexier,” Fox said.
 “They’re cooler bosses, aren’t they?” Renaux said. “Yeah. I think that’s why he grows to love it there.”
 Photo: HBO 
 Did Morgan and Carla get back together?
 Nope! Even though our final glimpse of Morgan and Carla are of them happily sharing time at the Normandy house, the divorce went through. They’re done, but they’re no longer enemies.
 “I think it was nice to see them,” Sienna Miller said. “It was bittersweet, they were war weary. It was nice to see them together. It was fun for Dom and I to do a scene that wasn’t acrimonious. But it could have ended a million different ways. What did you think about the ending?” 
 “I thought, ‘What a waste of 10 million.’ Imagine spending all that on lawyers!” Dominic West said. “But maybe that’s what they had to go through, or he had to go through, or they had to go through, to come out the other side as friends.” 
 Will there be a War Season 2 on HBO?
 Yes! War has already been picked up for a second season. Marisa Tomei and Kelly Macdonald join the cast as two former co-workers locked in a bitter defamation case. 
 “In season two of War , it’s about a libel case, a defamation case, and so it becomes about reputation,” Kay said. “Not just the reputation of Marisa Tomei and Kelly McDonald in the case of Season 2, but also our reputations with each other as we find out things about our work or how we’re being perceived by others. So reputation becomes the theme.”
